plan.question: My hypothesis: the podocytes this atlas calls 'endocytic' really carry LRP2, and the UMOD seen in B cells is spillover from neighbouring thick ascending limb cells. Does each part hold up under stricter assignment?
plan.summary: Two assignment audits cover both testable parts across all 21 distinct sections, excluding duplicate GSM8720419. Left out: direct verification of the atlas's original 'endocytic' podocyte annotation, because deposited author cell-type labels are unavailable; the NPHS1-anchored rule provides the supported non-circular podocyte proxy.

steps.rationale: Testing LRP2 in NPHS1-anchored podocytes, whose membership ignores LRP2 and CUBN, avoids defining the population by the gene being audited.
Testing UMOD retention in default-labelled B cells under nucleus-only and distance-capped assignment directly assesses the proposed TAL spillover signal.

sub_claims.text: Podocytes described as endocytic genuinely carry LRP2, so LRP2 expression should remain under stricter molecule assignment.
UMOD observed in B cells is spillover from neighbouring TAL cells, so B-cell UMOD expression should fall under stricter molecule assignment.

verdict.question: My hypothesis: the podocytes this atlas calls 'endocytic' really carry LRP2, and the UMOD seen in B cells is spillover from neighbouring thick ascending limb cells. Does each part hold up under stricter assignment?
verdict.scope: In these sections and regions, under the controls each claim cites. A verdict says what this evidence supports, not whether the biology is true.

sub_claim.text: Podocytes described as endocytic genuinely carry LRP2, so LRP2 expression should remain under stricter molecule assignment.
UMOD observed in B cells is spillover from neighbouring TAL cells, so B-cell UMOD expression should fall under stricter molecule assignment.

verdict.rule: A sub-claim rests on the non-injected claims about its cell type and any of its genes. Each verified claim's outcome is 'holds' when its evidence label is stable and 'drops' when it is segmentation-sensitive. Confirmed: every claim is verified with an outcome, and every outcome is the predicted one. Refuted: every claim is verified with an outcome, and every outcome is the opposite. Inconclusive: no claim, a claim that is not verified (failed, disputed, unavailable or pending), insufficient evidence, or outcomes that disagree.
